title: Crossbuns. One meal
html_source: A crossbun is a pastry usually eaten hot, containing spices and raisins with a cross on the top to signify the crucifixion of Jesus. Typically eaten on Good Friday by Christians. Here Joyce contrasts two religious holidays, Yom Kippur, a day of fasting, prayer and atonement, and Good Friday. Although the Catholic Church treats Good Friday as a fast day, this is understood as having only one full meal and two collations (a smaller repast) and on which the faithful abstain from eating meat. This is why many places have the typical ‘Fish Friday’. Here again Bloom, when he says `for fear he’d collapse..‘ is implying that Catholics are unable, possibly too weak, to fast as Jews do.
